crlf_mechanics: ledger_lines() skips the header by prefix match (source_path + TAB), so a CRLF header is skipped like an LF one.
try_obsidian() reads each row with IFS=TAB and read -r sp ss vp vs _rest; the trailing CR is not TAB-separated, so it stays attached to the LAST field of the row.
In the canonical 6-column row the last field is note, absorbed by _rest; vault_sha256 (field 4) stays clean -> the row matches -> SAFE(moved-to-obsidian) / VERIFIED(moved-to-obsidian).

Only when the row is truncated to 4 columns does the CR land on vault_sha256 itself -> digest comparison fails. That is the break boundary this case pins; whether a candidate recovers from it is schema-tolerance, not a requirement, so it is declared informational.

notes_for_parent: case-V6 is consumable by all three V-family runners: probes[] for runner-26, targets[]+expect[] for runner-28/29, plus the --out/--ledger/--quiet builder contract they invoke.

The judged probes are crlf-valid-row and lf-control (both must verify). The truncated-CRLF probe is informational by design: impl-24 legitimately verifies it by stripping CR, so requiring NOT-VERIFIED there would falsely fail a conforming harness.

The CRLF bytes round-trip through git unchanged: the lane repo has no .gitattributes and core.autocrlf is unset. The case .gitignore keeps in-place materialization untracked, so the tracked case dir holds only make-fixture.sh, selftest.sh, expected.json, README.md and .gitignore.
The builder must be re-run before runners: both modes regenerate ledgers with the current root paths (ledger rows embed absolute paths).
